title: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh calls for enhancing Private Sector Participation in India’s Biotechnology Ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh calls for enhancing Private Sector Participation in India’s Biotechnology Ecosystem Government Steps Up Efforts to Build Globally Competitive Biotechnology Ecosystem: Dr Jitendra Singh Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises Stronger Industry Outreach to Promote Indigenous Biotechnology Products and Mobilise Investment BIRAC-RDIF to Accelerate Commercialisation of Indigenous Biotechnology Innovations with Support of ₹5200 Crore BIRAC to Strengthen Industry Linkages through Life Sciences GCCs, CSR Partnerships and Startup-Investor Connect प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh has called for enhancing private sector participation in India’s Biotechnology ecosystem, strengthening thr industry outreach to promote indigenous products and technologies in biotechnology and life sciences, and to encourage greater private investment. Dr Jitendra Singh stressed the need to build stronger linkages between India’s indigenous biotechnology capabilities, industry and investors so that promising innovations can move from research and development to commercialisation at a faster pace. The Minister’s emphasis came during a meeting with senior officials of the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) in New Delhi, where a range of measures to expand investment, industry participation and market opportunities for India’s biotechnology ecosystem were discussed. The meeting focused on the implementation of the BIRAC Research, Development and Innovation Fund (BIRAC-RDIF), strengthening industry engagement in biotechnology, integrating Life Sciences Global Capability Centres (GCCs) with the domestic biotech ecosystem, leveraging Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) for biotechnology-led initiatives, enhancing BIRAC’s outreach and international visibility, and creating stronger investor linkages for biotechnology startups and enterprises. Dr. Dhananjay Tiwary, Managing Director, BIRAC and Senior Adviser/Scientist ‘H’, DBT; Dr. Manish Diwan, Group General Manager and Head, BIRAC-RDIF; CS Kavita Anandani, General Manager and Head, Corporate & Legal Affairs along with senior officials were present. The BIRAC-RDIF is a key component of the Government of India’s ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund aimed at advancing deep-tech innovations and high-impact indigenous manufacturing under the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on November 3, 2025, the RDI Fund is managed by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) and the Department of Science and Technology (DST), with BIRAC designated as a Second Level Fund Manager for the biotechnology sector. BIRAC-RDIF is designed to support the development and commercialisation of indigenous biotechnology innovations, particularly high-risk and technology-intensive projects spanning Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 4 to 9. Eligible technology entities, including startups and industry, can receive assistance ranging from ₹5 crore to ₹200 crore, covering up to 50 per cent of the total project cost. The Fund provides support through collateral-free long-term loans, equity and hybrid instruments, with a strategic co-investment framework aimed at catalysing greater private-sector participation in biotechnology. BIRAC has established a dedicated BIRAC-RDIF division to ensure ring-fenced implementation of the Fund. The first National Call for Proposals was launched on February 13, 2026, along with the BIRAC-RDIF website and an integrated e-portal for receiving applications from eligible startups and industry. A total of 198 applications has been received and are being appraised in accordance with the scheme guidelines. Screening and evaluation of the first 50 applications has been completed, with eight Eligible Technology Entities selected so far on the recommendations of the Investment Committee comprising external experts. These entities are currently undergoing detailed due diligence before entering into loan or equity agreements. The meeting also focused on tapping the growing Life Sciences Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem to deepen industry participation in India’s biotechnology sector. India currently hosts more than 1,700 GCCs employing around 1.9 million professionals, while life sciences and healthcare GCCs have emerged as important centres of R&D in areas including biopharmaceuticals, medical devices and digital health. BIRAC will facilitate greater integration of existing and prospective GCCs with the domestic biotechnology ecosystem by mapping their requirements in infrastructure, pilot-scale manufacturing and R&D, and connecting them with India’s BioE3 bio-foundries, bio-incubators and StartUps. The role of CSR in expanding the biotechnology ecosystem was also taken up during the meeting. With India’s CSR expenditure increasing substantially over the past decade and healthcare accounting for a significant share of CSR investments, BIRAC proposes to leverage its scientific due-diligence capabilities, nationwide network and transparent grant-management framework to channel CSR investments into biotechnology-led social innovation. Areas identified include affordable healthcare, diagnostics, maternal and child health, nutrition, climate-resilient agriculture and skill development. BIRAC already has a CSR-implementing-agency framework and has undertaken pilot corporate CSR initiatives, providing a foundation for scaling up such partnerships. Strengthening BIRAC’s outreach and visibility was another area of focus. BIRAC has proposed branding initiatives at Jammu and Vadodara airports to showcase DBT-BIRAC achievements and create greater awareness among corporates, investors and global partners about opportunities to collaborate with India’s biotechnology ecosystem. Jammu is emerging as a destination for biotech, healthcare and Agri-innovation, while Vadodara has an established pharma-biotech-manufacturing base. The meeting also addressed the need to strengthen India’s biotechnology investment ecosystem, particularly access to growth-stage capital. In this context, BIRAC has proposed the BIRAC Startup Investor Connect, a dedicated platform to bring together investment-ready biotechnology startups and investors. The platform is envisaged to create greater awareness of biotechnology opportunities, facilitate strategic partnerships, strengthen investment networks and accelerate the commercialisation of innovative technologies. The initiatives discussed during the meeting seek to strengthen the bridge between India’s scientific capabilities, indigenous biotechnology products, industry and investment, while creating greater opportunities for public and private sector participation. The approach is aimed at accelerating the journey of Indian biotechnology innovations from laboratory validation to commercialisation and strengthening the foundation for a globally competitive biotechnology ecosystem aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. ***** NKR/AK/MJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297115) आगंतुक पटल  : 165 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Gujarati Ministry of Science & Technology Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh calls for enhancing Private Sector Participation in India’s Biotechnology Ecosystem Government Steps Up Efforts to Build Globally Competitive Biotechnology Ecosystem: Dr Jitendra Singh Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises Stronger Industry Outreach to Promote Indigenous Biotechnology Products and Mobilise Investment BIRAC-RDIF to Accelerate Commercialisation of Indigenous Biotechnology Innovations with Support of ₹5200 Crore BIRAC to Strengthen Industry Linkages through Life Sciences GCCs, CSR Partnerships and Startup-Investor Connect प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on November 3, 2025, the RDI Fund is managed by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) and the Department of Science and Technology (DST), with BIRAC designated as a Second Level Fund Manager for the biotechnology sector. BIRAC-RDIF is designed to support the development and commercialisation of indigenous biotechnology innovations, particularly high-risk and technology-intensive projects spanning Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 4 to 9. Eligible technology entities, including startups and industry, can receive assistance ranging from ₹5 crore to ₹200 crore, covering up to 50 per cent of the total project cost. The Fund provides support through collateral-free long-term loans, equity and hybrid instruments, with a strategic co-investment framework aimed at catalysing greater private-sector participation in biotechnology. BIRAC has established a dedicated BIRAC-RDIF division to ensure ring-fenced implementation of the Fund. The first National Call for Proposals was launched on February 13, 2026, along with the BIRAC-RDIF website and an integrated e-portal for receiving applications from eligible startups and industry. A total of 198 applications has been received and are being appraised in accordance with the scheme guidelines. Screening and evaluation of the first 50 applications has been completed, with eight Eligible Technology Entities selected so far on the recommendations of the Investment Committee comprising external experts. These entities are currently undergoing detailed due diligence before entering into loan or equity agreements. The meeting also focused on tapping the growing Life Sciences Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem to deepen industry participation in India’s biotechnology sector. India currently hosts more than 1,700 GCCs employing around 1.9 million professionals, while life sciences and healthcare GCCs have emerged as important centres of R&D in areas including biopharmaceuticals, medical devices and digital health. BIRAC will facilitate greater integration of existing and prospective GCCs with the domestic biotechnology ecosystem by mapping their requirements in infrastructure, pilot-scale manufacturing and R&D, and connecting them with India’s BioE3 bio-foundries, bio-incubators and StartUps. The role of CSR in expanding the biotechnology ecosystem was also taken up during the meeting. With India’s CSR expenditure increasing substantially over the past decade and healthcare accounting for a significant share of CSR investments, BIRAC proposes to leverage its scientific due-diligence capabilities, nationwide network and transparent grant-management framework to channel CSR investments into biotechnology-led social innovation. Areas identified include affordable healthcare, diagnostics, maternal and child health, nutrition, climate-resilient agriculture and skill development. BIRAC already has a CSR-implementing-agency framework and has undertaken pilot corporate CSR initiatives, providing a foundation for scaling up such partnerships. Strengthening BIRAC’s outreach and visibility was another area of focus. BIRAC has proposed branding initiatives at Jammu and Vadodara airports to showcase DBT-BIRAC achievements and create greater awareness among corporates, investors and global partners about opportunities to collaborate with India’s biotechnology ecosystem. Jammu is emerging as a destination for biotech, healthcare and Agri-innovation, while Vadodara has an established pharma-biotech-manufacturing base. The meeting also addressed the need to strengthen India’s biotechnology investment ecosystem, particularly access to growth-stage capital. In this context, BIRAC has proposed the BIRAC Startup Investor Connect, a dedicated platform to bring together investment-ready biotechnology startups and investors. The platform is envisaged to create greater awareness of biotechnology opportunities, facilitate strategic partnerships, strengthen investment networks and accelerate the commercialisation of innovative technologies. The initiatives discussed during the meeting seek to strengthen the bridge between India’s scientific capabilities, indigenous biotechnology products, industry and investment, while creating greater opportunities for public and private sector participation. The approach is aimed at accelerating the journey of Indian biotechnology innovations from laboratory validation to commercialisation and strengthening the foundation for a globally competitive biotechnology ecosystem aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. ***** NKR/AK/MJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297115)

title: TDB-DST Supports M/s Griva Healthcare Pvt. Ltd., Vishakhapatnam for Commercialization of Indigenous AI-Powered Cervical Cancer Screening Technology
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s Griva Healthcare Pvt. Ltd., Vishakhapatnam for Commercialization of Indigenous AI-Powered Cervical Cancer Screening Technology प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi With early and accessible screening being critical to reducing the burden of cervical cancer among women, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, today entered into an agreement with M/s Griva Healthcare Pvt. Ltd., Vishakhapatnamto support the manufacturing and commercialization of ‘GrivaVision’, an indigenously developed, portable digital colposcope with AI-assisted capabilities for early detection of cervical pre-cancerous lesions. Through TDB’s support, the company will establish manufacturing capabilities at Kollam, Kerala, enabling commercial-scale production and wider deployment of the technology. The initiative seeks to make cervical cancer screening more accessible and affordable, particularly across primary and community healthcare settings, while strengthening domestic capabilities in advanced medical devices and reducing dependence on imported diagnostic equipment. GrivaVision integrates a high-definition camera, in-built display, user-friendly interface, advanced optics, and indigenous AI-enabled software into a portable diagnostic platform. Designed for visualization of the vaginal canal and examination of cervical lesions, the system assists gynaecologists in identifying pre-cancerous abnormalities during routine clinical examinations. The technology is designed in accordance with WHO-approved Automated Visual Evaluation (AVE) standards and its software is ABDM-compliant, enabling integration with India's evolving digital health ecosystem. The product is classified as a Class B non-invasive medical device and carries a CDSCO Class B manufacturing licence. It is being developed in accordance with ISO 13485 quality standards. The hardware architecture is proprietary and has been patented in India by Griva Healthcare. The company is presently undertaking its R&D activities at AIC-AMTZ Medivalley, Visakhapatnam, with the TDB-supported project enabling transition towards commercial manufacturing at its upcoming facility in Kerala. A key feature of the project is its focus on indigenous development and localization. The technology has been developed and built in India, with more than 50% of product components currently sourced indigenously. Commercialization at scale is expected to further strengthen the domestic medical device value chain and create a cost-effective Indian alternative in cervical cancer diagnostics. The technology assumes particular relevance considering the large population of women eligible for cervical cancer screening in India. By combining portability, digital imaging, AI-assisted assessment, and ease of deployment, GrivaVision has the potential to extend screening beyond specialized healthcare facilities and support healthcare professionals in reaching women in underserved and resource-constrained regions. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, stated, “Early detection can make a decisive difference in addressing cervical cancer. Indigenous technologies such as GrivaVision demonstrate how medical devices, digital health and artificial intelligence can come together to address a critical healthcare need at scale. TDB’s support is aimed at taking such home-grown innovations from technology development to commercial manufacturing, making advanced screening solutions more accessible while strengthening India’s self-reliance in medical technologies.” Expressing gratitude for TDB’s support, the leadership of Griva Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. stated that the assistance will enable the company to transition its indigenous technology to commercial-scale manufacturing and expand access to AI-assisted cervical cancer screening. The company noted that its endeavour is to make reliable screening technology available closer to women, particularly in regions where access to specialized diagnostic infrastructure remains limited. *** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297106) आगंतुक पटल  : 183 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s Griva Healthcare Pvt. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship New-Age Skills Under PMKVY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi State/ UT-wise number of candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) during the last five years and the current year, including in Tamil Nadu, is given at Annexure. The PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and there is no provision for State-wise fund allocation. However, in the last three years starting from FY 2022-23 and in the current FY 2026-27, ₹2,392.37 crore has been released for implementation of the scheme. Under PMKVY 4.0, training has been standardized through the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), aligning courses with industry needs and national priorities. Under the Scheme, training has been aligned to the requirements of new-age and futuristic job roles such as AI, Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), Semiconductor, Drone technology, Solar, 3D Printing, etc. as per changing requirement and market demand. To meet emerging technology demands, 600+ new-age and futuristic courses have been introduced. As on 30.06.2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained/oriented in new-age and futuristic job roles under PMKVY 4.0 across the country. PMKVY is a demand driven scheme accessible to every section of society including Women, Scheduled Castes (SCs)/ Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other marginalized communities. The Scheme has a provision of Special Projects which are targeted towards ensuring coverage of under-represented social groups - SC/ ST/ Women/ PwDs and geographic areas such as Aspirational Districts, Tribal districts, etc. Special attention has been given to women, tribal communities, and other marginalized groups in rural areas to promote their participation in the skill development programs. In order to improve inclusivity by ensuring that SC, ST, women, and other marginalized communities can undertake skill training and eventually access gainful wage and self-employment, boarding & lodging and transportation facilities are provided as per Common Norms. For non-residential training, conveyance/ transportation costs are covered for women and PwDs. Additionally, ₹5,000 is provided for assistive devices, aids, and appliances for PwD candidates. All candidates are also covered under one-year accidental insurance for additional social protection. title: Assessment of Skill Development Initiatives
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Assessment of Skill Development Initiatives प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS),National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Chhattisgarh. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills. State/UT-wise, year-wise and scheme-wise details of the number of candidates trained across the country under the major skill development schemes of MSDE during the period from 2019–20 to 2026–27 (as on 30.06.2026) are given at Annexures I to IV . Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short-Term Training component of PMKVY only in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) implemented from 2015-16 to 2021-22. Under PMKVY (1.0 to 3.0), 28,142 candidates have been reported placed in Chhattisgarh. Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career path with orientation through industry relevant skill courses that include the On-the-Job Training (OJT). The Government undertakes periodic reviews of skilling initiatives under the Skill India Mission, assessing enrolment, certification, placement, self-employment outcomes and employer feedback to gauge their effectiveness in strengthening employability and future skills. These reviews support continuous curriculum updates, industry collaboration and improvements in implementation modalities, ensuring that skilling programmes remain aligned with evolving technology trends and labour-market requirements. The effectiveness of broader skill development schemes is also evaluated through MIS-based monitoring, third-party assessments and beneficiary feedback. All schemes presently being run by MSDE have gone through third party evaluation exercise generally and also in particular, at the time of grant of extension of the respective schemes. Details of the evaluation of the Schemes implemented by MSDE are as under: PMKVY 4.0: An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. JSS : A third-party evaluation of the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme was conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management, an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India, in 2025 to assess the scheme’s outreach, effectiveness and livelihood outcomes. The evaluation highlighted significant achievements of the scheme, with 33.94 lakh individuals enrolled, of whom 32 lakh were trained and 31.52 lakh certified, reflecting an overall success rate of 99 percent. Women constituted a dominant 82 percent share of total participants, while 73 percent beneficiaries belonged to marginalized sections, including SC/ST (36 percent) and OBC (37 percent). The livelihood impact has been noteworthy, with 90 percent alumni utilising acquired skills for income generation, 82 percent becoming economically engaged within six months of training, and 60 percent of previously non-earning individuals starting to earn post-training. The average monthly income of beneficiaries recorded a four-fold increase. NAPS: A third-party evaluation study of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (PMNAPS-2) from 2022-23 to 2025-26 (Data up to 30 th November 2025) was conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMNAPS-2 achieved significant scale during the evaluation period, engaging 34.69 lakh apprentices against a cumulative target of 46 lakh, translating into an overall achievement of approximately 75 percent. The institutionalization of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) has improved financial transparency and predictability.                         10 AUG 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS),National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Chhattisgarh. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills. State/UT-wise, year-wise and scheme-wise details of the number of candidates trained across the country under the major skill development schemes of MSDE during the period from 2019–20 to 2026–27 (as on 30.06.2026) are given at Annexures I to IV . Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short-Term Training component of PMKVY only in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) implemented from 2015-16 to 2021-22. Under PMKVY (1.0 to 3.0), 28,142 candidates have been reported placed in Chhattisgarh. Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career path with orientation through industry relevant skill courses that include the On-the-Job Training (OJT). The Government undertakes periodic reviews of skilling initiatives under the Skill India Mission, assessing enrolment, certification, placement, self-employment outcomes and employer feedback to gauge their effectiveness in strengthening employability and future skills. These reviews support continuous curriculum updates, industry collaboration and improvements in implementation modalities, ensuring that skilling programmes remain aligned with evolving technology trends and labour-market requirements. The effectiveness of broader skill development schemes is also evaluated through MIS-based monitoring, third-party assessments and beneficiary feedback. All schemes presently being run by MSDE have gone through third party evaluation exercise generally and also in particular, at the time of grant of extension of the respective schemes. Details of the evaluation of the Schemes implemented by MSDE are as under: PMKVY 4.0: An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. JSS : A third-party evaluation of the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme was conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management, an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India, in 2025 to assess the scheme’s outreach, effectiveness and livelihood outcomes. The evaluation highlighted significant achievements of the scheme, with 33.94 lakh individuals enrolled, of whom 32 lakh were trained and 31.52 lakh certified, reflecting an overall success rate of 99 percent. Women constituted a dominant 82 percent share of total participants, while 73 percent beneficiaries belonged to marginalized sections, including SC/ST (36 percent) and OBC (37 percent). The livelihood impact has been noteworthy, with 90 percent alumni utilising acquired skills for income generation, 82 percent becoming economically engaged within six months of training, and 60 percent of previously non-earning individuals starting to earn post-training. The average monthly income of beneficiaries recorded a four-fold increase. NAPS: A third-party evaluation study of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (PMNAPS-2) from 2022-23 to 2025-26 (Data up to 30 th November 2025) was conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMNAPS-2 achieved significant scale during the evaluation period, engaging 34.69 lakh apprentices against a cumulative target of 46 lakh, translating into an overall achievement of approximately 75 percent. The institutionalization of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) has improved financial transparency and predictability.                 10 AUG 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022-23, the focus is on imparting training in emerging and new-age courses such as Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, green energy, electric vehicles, drones, cybersecurity, robotics, etc., as per the industry requirement. To meet emerging technology demands, 600+ new-age and futuristic courses have been introduced. As on 30.06.2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in new-age and futuristic job roles under PMKVY 4.0 across the country. Under PMKVY scheme, placements were tracked in the Short-Term Training (STT) component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, implemented from FY 2015-16 to FY 2021-22. In these versions of PMKVY, out of 56.89 lakh candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.37 lakh candidates were reported placed which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022-23, the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through On-Job Training (OJT) embedded industry relevant skill courses. PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across several states. As per the study, about 94% of the employers surveyed reported they would hire more candidates trained under PMKVY. Further, 52% of the candidates who were placed in full time/part-time employment and oriented under the RPL component received higher salary or felt that they will get higher salary compared to their un-certified peers. Also, a third-party impact evaluation of PMKVY 2.0 (2016-20) was also conducted by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received placement in their desired skill sector. Further, a third-party evaluation of PMKVY 4.0 conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) in 2025 observed that PMKVY training has led to a measurable improvement in employment outcomes for Short-Term Training (STT) candidates, with the combined share of employed and self-employed respondents increasing from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% post-training, reflecting a significant rise of 18.8 % points. Moreover, 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates reported an increase in income following PMKVY training and certification. Year and State/UT-wise number of candidates trained and certified under the PMKVY during the last three years and the current year (up to 30.06.2026) are given at Annexure I and Sector-wise details are given at Annexure II . PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and there is no provision of State-wise fund allocation. The Year-wise details of funds allocated and released for implementation of PMKVY 4.0 during the last three years and the current year (up to 30.06.2026) are given below: (₹ in crore) FY Budget Estimate Revised Estimate Funds Released 2023-24 1,558.00 920.00 510.52 2024-25 1,938.30 1,538.00 1,538.00 2025-26 1,915.00 1,100.00 265.57 2026-27 1,400.00 - 78.28 Total 6,811.30 3,558.00 2,392.37 The State/UT-wise and FY-wise utilization of funds for implementation of PMKVY 4.0 during the last three years and the current year is given at Annexure III . Under PMKVY, industries play a vital role in imparting quality skilling in the country. The training has been standardized through the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), aligning courses with industry needs and national priorities. Industry-led Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) engage with industries to identify skill gaps, develop curriculum, define competency standards, and oversee training, assessment, and certification in alignment with NSQF. A major reform is the integration of On-the-Job Training (OJT) through industries, ensuring real-world industry exposure. Moreover, more than fifteen industries have been designated as Awarding Bodies (ABs) to develop job roles aligned with industry needs such as HCL Technologies, IBM, Bajaj Finserv, Microsoft, etc. In collaboration with industries, Kaushal Mahotsavs are organized to provide employment opportunities to the skilled candidates. Additionally, various industries have been onboarded under the Scheme to deliver skill training across sectors. Additionally, the Ministry has launched the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a unified digital platform that integrates the skilling, education, employment and entrepreneurship ecosystems to provide lifelong access to a wide range of services. Details of trained candidates are available on the platform, enabling potential employers to identify and connect with suitably skilled candidates. SIDH also facilitates access to employment and apprenticeship opportunities by connecting candidates with prospective employers and establishments.                 10 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), Directorate General of Training (DGT) and under PMKVY 4.0, has initiated multiple programmes for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based training and skilling across sectors: 1. Under the NCVET-regulated ecosystem, 116 NSQF-aligned and NSQC-approved Qualifications, National Occupational Standards (NOSs) and Micro-Credentials relating to Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are presently in place, covering domains such as Generative AI, Agentic AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Engineering, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, Robotics and Automation, AI Security, AI Ethics, AI Governance, and sector-specific AI applications. 2. Under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, training is imparted in AI and AI-enabled job roles across sectors such as IT-ITES, Telecom and Life Sciences, with job roles developed in consultation with industry and Sector Skill Councils. As of 30.06.2026 under PMKVY 4.0, 53,449 candidates been trained/oriented and 25,466 candidates certified in AI related job roles. 3. The Directorate General of Training (DGT) has introduced AI into vocational training through the Artificial Intelligence Programming Assistant (1-year) course, a 240-hour Generative AI course, and a 7.5-hour AI micro-credential for trainees in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). The compulsory Employability Skills curriculum has also been revised to include modules on AI and Green Skills. A list of 32 new-age courses introduced across ITIs/NSTIs, including AI-related trades, is at Annexure-I , with trade-wise enrolment for the period 2021-2025 at Annexure-II . The schemes, partnerships and platforms developed to impart AI-related skills are as under. A specific assessment of demand for AI-related skills and the current workforce gap has not been done; the schemes below are, however, designed on a demand-driven and industry-aligned basis, as indicated against each: 1. Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR): Launched by NCVET to promote AI literacy, initially with four foundational courses - AI to be Aware, AI to Acquire, AI to Aspire and AI for Educators - subsequently expanded to 50 AI and AI-application-oriented NSQF-aligned courses covering AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications and inclusivity. Courses are delivered through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) by NCVET-recognised Awarding Bodies. 2. PMKVY 4.0: Designed as a demand-driven, industry-aligned scheme, with training programmes and job roles identified in consultation with industry and Sector Skill Councils to address evolving workforce requirements in emerging technologies. AI-related training is delivered through a network of AICTE-affiliated colleges, private universities/colleges, engineering colleges, ITIs, NIELIT centres, PMKKs, Skill Universities, Institutes of National Importance, and State Government universities/colleges. 3. DGT: Industry partnerships: In collaboration with Microsoft and the Edunet Foundation, the Artificial Intelligence Programming Assistant (AIPA) course under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) was implemented at 19 National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) in the 2024-25 session (intake capacity 504), and extended to 23 NSTIs in 2025-26 (intake capacity 600). Institute-wise details are at Annexure-III . Steps taken to ensure inclusive access to AI-based training are as below: 1. SOAR has been designed for inclusive access through fully online, self-paced courses delivered on SIDH, enabling youth, educators and other learners - including those from rural and semi-urban areas - to acquire nationally recognized, NSQF-aligned and credit-linked AI competencies through a flexible digital learning mode. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 4,96,426 learners have enrolled and 98,576 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH). 2. PMKVY 4.0 training has been extended to rural, semi-urban, aspirational and underserved districts, covering AI, Machine Learning, Data Analytics, IoT, Drones, Semiconductors, Electric Vehicles, Green Hydrogen, Renewable Energy, Robotics and 5G Technologies, delivered through a wide network of training institutions across States and Union Territories. As of 30.06.2026 under PMKVY 4.0, 53,449 candidates been trained/oriented and 25,466 candidates certified in AI related job roles. Details are kept at Annexure IV . title: ITI Upgradation and Industry Alignment Under PM-SETU
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship ITI Upgradation and Industry Alignment Under PM-SETU प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme envisages to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training with upgraded labs, machines, and industry-aligned curriculum in the country. The key objectives of the scheme are as under: To improve the quality of training delivery in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs); To modernize infrastructure and equipment as per industry standards; To introduce industry-aligned long-term and short-term courses, especially in new and emerging sectors; To strengthen industry linkage for demand-driven skilling and better employment outcomes; and To enhance the capacity of NSTIs for training of trainers. The scheme comprises of two components: Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new courses aligned to industry needs. Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership. The selection criteria for Government ITIs to be included under the Scheme is decided by the States/ Union Territories (UTs) in consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill needs and local industrial potential. States/ UTs through their respective Steering Committees have the flexibility to fix appropriate eligibility criteria, such as turnover and number of employees, at the Expression of Interest (EOI) or Request for Proposal (RFP) stage, based on their local context and industrial landscape. States/ UTs accordingly invite industry participation, and industry, in response, submits a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) for the approval of the State Steering Committee and the National Steering Committee (NSC). Upon approval, the selected industry is required to form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). The SIPs are approved on a first-come-first-serve basis, subject to completion of the prescribed technical and financial evaluation process and therefore the question of disparity does not arise. So far, Seven (07) SIPs submitted by Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs), comprising Three from Telangana, One from Andhra Pradesh, One from Rajasthan, One from Odisha and One from Gujarat is approved. The details of the approved clusters are provided in Annexure I . The curriculum review and revision process is a continuous and need-based exercise aimed at ensuring alignment with technological advancements and evolving industry requirements. The evaluation involves assessment of existing curricula with respect to emerging technologies, changing occupational standards, industry demand, employability trends, apprenticeship requirements, training outcomes, and feedback received during implementation. The curriculum revision process involves extensive consultations with stakeholders including State Governments/ UT Administrations, industry representatives, Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), NSTIs, subject matter experts, academia, employers, implementing agencies and other concerned Ministries/ Departments, wherever required. Based on the evaluation and stakeholder consultations, curricula are revised to incorporate new technologies, Industry 4.0 applications, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), automation, green and renewable energy technologies, electric mobility, digital skills, entrepreneurship, workplace safety, environmental sustainability and outcome-based learning. The Directorate General of Training (DGT) has introduced 32 new-age courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), the details of which are provided in Annexure II . Since ITIs are under the administrative and financial control of State Governments, States may adopt these courses in their ITIs. The industry-led SPVs under the Scheme leads the upgradation and are empowered to propose necessary interventions relating to curriculum redesign, training delivery models, infrastructure upgradation, industry exposure in alignment with local industry needs and the Scheme guidelines. The Scheme aims to enhance employability by equipping learners with industry-relevant skills, facilitating apprenticeships and practical workplace exposure, and providing access to career guidance, placement support, and self-employment opportunities through industry-led governance framework. The focus of the scheme is to equip trainees with industry-relevant skills in emerging sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), semiconductors, green energy, and other high-growth industrial sectors. The scheme has been approved to be implemented over a period of five years. Annexure-I Annexure I: Details of approved Cluster S. NAVYA programme is being implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (PMKVY 4.0). The programme focuses on empowering trained candidates to pursue diverse career pathways by providing industry-relevant skill courses with embedded On-the-Job Training (OJT). Under NAVYA, special emphasis is placed on training in futuristic job roles, along with a mandatory Holistic Development Module covering digital literacy, financial literacy, career readiness, and entrepreneurship orientation etc. These interventions enhance the employability, economic participation, and overall career preparedness of adolescent girls. The Government monitors and evaluates the implementation and outcomes of the Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls (NAVYA) programme through a robust monitoring framework under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). Regular review meetings are conducted with Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), State Skill Development Missions (SSDMs) and other stakeholders to assess progress and address implementation-related issues. title: PM-YASASVI Scheme Implementation in Maharashtra Reviewed Regularly; Corrective Measures Undertaken to Improve Scholarship Coverage
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment PM-YASASVI Scheme Implementation in Maharashtra Reviewed Regularly; Corrective Measures Undertaken to Improve Scholarship Coverage ₹1,940 Lakh Released Under Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme in Maharashtra During 2025-26 Posted On:
                10 AUG 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government has stated that the implementation of the PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme in Maharashtra is regularly reviewed through monthly video conferences as well as regional and national-level conferences. The written reply was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma in response to questions by Shri Bhaskar Murlidhar Bhagare, Smt Supriya Sule, Prof Varsha Eknath Gaikwad, Shri Mohite Patil Dhairyasheel Rajsinh and Dr Amol Ramsing Kolhe in the Lok Lok Sabha. The PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme comprises the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, Top Class Education in Schools for OBCs and others, and Top Class Education in Colleges for OBCs and others. The Minister said that for the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes, the Central Government provides funds to the implementing States and Union Territories on the basis of approved notional allocation, while selection, verification and disbursement of scholarships to eligible beneficiaries are carried out by the respective States and Union Territories. Shri Verma stated that Maharashtra was onboarded on the National Scholarship Portal for both the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric OBC Scholarship Schemes from the Academic Year 2025-26 onwards. As per the information provided, during FY 2025-26, 1,079 applications were received under the PM-YASASVI Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students in Maharashtra. Of these, 1,072 applications were Aadhaar verified and 575 applications were verified. Under the PM-YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students, 1,971 applications were received during FY 2025-26. Of these, 1,965 were Aadhaar verified and 576 applications were verified. The Minister further stated that the Government released ₹555.74 lakh to the State Government of Maharashtra under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students during 2024-25, increasing to ₹1,940 lakh during 2025-26. No proposal was received from the State in FY 2023-24 and, therefore, no funds were released during that year. For the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, no Central Assistance was released during the last three financial years. The reply stated that this was due to non-receipt of proposals in FY 2023-24, pending unutilised balance in the State's SNA account in FY 2024-25, and a technical issue in disbursing funds by the State Government of Maharashtra during FY 2025-26. Under the Top Class Education in Schools Scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, 3,470 fresh applications were received in 2023-24, of which 2,324 were finally verified. In 2024-25, 2,192 fresh applications were received, with 1,195 finally verified. In 2025-26, 8,402 fresh applications were received, of which 4,533 were finally verified. Funds released to Maharashtra under the Top Class Education in Schools Scheme increased from ₹52.31 lakh in 2023-24 to ₹258.55 lakh in 2024-25 and ₹509.37 lakh in 2025-26. Under the Top Class Education in Colleges Scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, 363 fresh applications were received and 342 were finally verified in 2023-24 . In 2024-25, 731 fresh applications were received, with 611 finally verified. Funds released under the Top Class Education in Colleges Scheme increased from ₹1,000.39 lakh in 2023-24 to ₹2,712.14 lakh in 2024-25 and ₹2,857.95 lakh in 2025-26. The Minister stated that necessary corrective measures have been undertaken to address the issue of low scholarship coverage in Maharashtra. These include creating awareness about the Scheme among eligible beneficiaries, coordinating closely with educational institutions and district authorities to improve outreach, and regularly monitoring the application and verification process to ensure timely and accurate disbursal. The Government has also stated that delays in disbursal mainly arise from incomplete proposals submitted by States/Union Territories, non-submission of Utilisation Certificates against funds already released, non-onboarding of certain States/Union Territories on the SNA-SPARSH platform and non-seeding of bank accounts with Aadhaar. States and Union Territories have been mandated to onboard the SNA-SPARSH platform to improve efficiency and transparency in fund disbursal through real-time, utilisation-based tracking of funds. The Government continues to pursue timely submission of proposals and Utilisation Certificates through regional and national-level review meetings and video conferences, with a focus on improving outreach, verification and timely scholarship disbursal under PM-YASASVI in Maharashtra. ***** PR-63-TAR-KV-GA (Release ID: 2297288) Visitor Counter : 66 Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment PM-YASASVI Scheme Implementation in Maharashtra Reviewed Regularly; Corrective Measures Undertaken to Improve Scholarship Coverage ₹1,940 Lakh Released Under Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme in Maharashtra During 2025-26 Posted On:

title: 2,824 Children Identified, Rescued and Rehabilitated under SMILE Scheme
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 2,824 Children Identified, Rescued and Rehabilitated under SMILE Scheme 1,549 Children Reunited with Parents/Families; 676 Admitted to Schools and 309 to Anganwadi Centres प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi The Government has informed the Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Central Sector Scheme, Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging , since 23rd October 2023 in 216 major cities and towns across 33 States/Union Territories. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma in response to a question by Dr Mohammad Jawed in Lok Sabha. Under the Scheme, data relating to persons, including children, identified as engaged in the act of begging is collected during surveys and rescue operations undertaken by the Implementing Authorities. Shri Verma said the Scheme accords special attention to children identified as engaged in the act of begging. Such children are reunited with their families, wherever feasible, or provided appropriate support through Anganwadi Centres and Schools. Children requiring institutional care are produced before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) and linked to Child Care Institutions (CCIs) under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the Minister further stated in the House. As on 30 June 2026 , a total of 2,824 children have been identified, rescued and rehabilitated under the Scheme. Of these, 1,549 children have been reunited with their parents/families , 309 children have been admitted to Anganwadi Centres , 290 children have been produced before the Child Welfare Committee , and 676 children have been admitted to Schools . The Government has stated that age-wise and gender-wise data of identified children are not maintained separately under the Scheme. The Government is not implementing any scheme specifically for children engaged in the act of begging. However, the SMILE – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging contains specific provisions for the identification, rescue, rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children engaged in begging through family reunification, admission to schools and Anganwadi Centres, or institutional care through Child Welfare Committees and Child Care Institutions, wherever required. The Scheme has specific and focused provisions for rehabilitation of children engaged in begging. Its framework provides for 100 per cent rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children surveyed, profiled and rescued from beggary . The Government has further stated that, since the ongoing SMILE Scheme has a specific focus on the rehabilitation and mainstreaming of children rescued from beggary, there is no need for a separate scheme for this purpose. As per the State-wise details, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number with 927 children identified and rehabilitated , followed by Chandigarh with 313 , Delhi with 233 , Maharashtra with 208 and Andhra Pradesh with 191 . **** PR-64-TAR-KV-GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297286) आगंतुक पटल  : 55 Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 2,824 Children Identified, Rescued and Rehabilitated under SMILE Scheme 1,549 Children Reunited with Parents/Families; 676 Admitted to Schools and 309 to Anganwadi Centres प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: From Financial Constraints to an Aspiration of Becoming an ISRO Scientist: How Scholarship Support Helped GANESH KUMAR Continue His Education
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Constraints to an Aspiration of Becoming an ISRO Scientist: How Scholarship Support Helped GANESH KUMAR Continue His Education प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi Access to quality education can play an important role in helping students pursue their aspirations and build better opportunities for the future. However, for students from economically constrained families, financial difficulties can become a major barrier to continuing college education and accessing the best available resources. Demonstrating how scholarship assistance can provide relief to students facing economic challenges, Mr Ganesh Kumar, a 19-year-old student belonging to the Other Backward Class (OBC) category , comes from a lower-middle-class family. His family faced economic problems, and he was not able to access the best resources for his education. Despite these challenges, Ganesh aspired to become an ISRO Scientist and remained focused on pursuing his education. The financial pressure associated with college fee submission created tension for Ganesh and his family. In 2026, scholarship assistance of ₹80,000 was provided to him. The support helped reduce the tension related to submission of his college fees and provided some relief from his economic problems. With the financial burden related to his college fees reduced, Ganesh has been able to continue his educational journey with greater relief from the immediate economic pressure. The scholarship support has helped address an important financial challenge and supported his pursuit of education while he works towards his aspiration of becoming an ISRO Scientist. Ganesh Kumar's story highlights how timely scholarship assistance can provide meaningful relief to students facing economic constraints. By helping reduce the financial pressure associated with college fee submission, the support has enabled him to continue his education and pursue his aspiration of contributing to India's scientific and space sector as an ISRO Scientist. **** SS-26-TAR-KV-GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297284) आगंतुक पटल  : 32 Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Constraints to an Aspiration of Becoming an ISRO Scientist: How Scholarship Support Helped GANESH KUMAR Continue His Education प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: From Financial Constraints to an MBA at IIM Raipur: PM-YASASVI Scholarship Supports Aitipamula Ooha’s Academic Aspirations
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Constraints to an MBA at IIM Raipur: PM-YASASVI Scholarship Supports Aitipamula Ooha’s Academic Aspirations प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi For talented students from economically disadvantaged families, securing admission to a premier institution is a major achievement, but the cost of higher education can remain a significant challenge. Ms Aitipamula Ooha, a 26-year-old student from the Other Backward Class (OBC) community, is pursuing her Master of Business Administration (MBA) at the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Raipur with financial support under the PM-YASASVI Scheme. Coming from a lower-middle-class family, Ooha grew up in circumstances where financial resources were limited. Her father is a photographer , and due to family responsibilities and the lack of a stable job, he continued working as a photographer throughout his life. Despite these circumstances, her parents were always keen on providing their children with education and encouraged Ooha to pursue her aspirations. Ooha has always aspired to become an administrative officer . Her determination to build a better future led her to pursue higher education, and she is currently working towards her MBA at IIM Raipur. While her immediate focus is on completing her MBA, she continues to keep her long-term aspiration of becoming an administrative officer. Securing admission to IIM Raipur was a significant achievement for Ooha and her family. However, the approximately ₹20 lakh fee associated with the MBA programme created a major financial challenge. To make her education possible, her family took a loan without collateral and hoped they would be able to manage the financial burden. The cost of education remained a source of concern even after she secured her place at the institution. During this period, Ooha came to know about the PM-YASASVI scholarship . She applied for the scholarship and received financial assistance of ₹10.27 lakh in April 2026. The support came at a crucial stage of her educational journey and provided substantial relief to her family. Reflecting on the support, Aitipamula Ooha said: "Securing my MBA seat was a very big thing for my family, but the fee of around ₹20 lakh was scary. We took a loan without any collateral and hoped for the best. When I received the PM-YASASVI scholarship, my family was very relieved. We are grateful for the support and hope that I can continue my studies without the burden of such financial pressure." Pursuing Higher Education with Greater Confidence With the financial burden reduced through the scholarship support, Ooha is now able to continue her MBA journey at IIM Raipur with greater confidence. The assistance has provided her family with much-needed relief at a time when financing higher education was a major concern. For Ooha, the scholarship represents more than financial assistance. It has helped ease the pressure on her family and strengthened their confidence in her educational journey. Coming from a family with limited financial resources, the opportunity to pursue an MBA at a premier institution is a significant milestone for her and her parents. Ooha’s journey demonstrates how timely educational support can help students overcome financial barriers and continue pursuing their aspirations. Her admission to IIM Raipur, combined with the support received under the PM-YASASVI Scheme, has enabled her to move forward with her higher education while reducing the financial burden on her family. Today, Ooha continues to pursue her MBA and work towards building a successful career. Her long-term aspiration of becoming an administrative officer remains an important goal, which she may pursue in the future. Her story reflects the determination of a young student and the role of educational assistance in ensuring that financial constraints do not stand in the way of academic aspirations. The success of Aitipamula Ooha demonstrates how the PM-YASASVI Scheme for Top Class Education for OBC, EBC and DNT Students is supporting deserving students in pursuing higher education. title: MoSPI signs two MoUs with IDEAS, ISI Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation MoSPI signs two MoUs with IDEAS, ISI Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies Posted On:
                10 AUG 2026 7:03PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Institute of Data Engineering, Analytics and Science Foundation (IDEAS), Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies. Shri Agnimitra Biswas, Chief Executive Officer, IDEAS and Shri Prasoon Verma, Director, Training Unit, Capacity Development Division, MoSPI signed the MoUs. The signing ceremony was graced by the presence of Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI and Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division, MoSPI. This collaborative initiative is an innovative, knowledge sharing platform between MoSPI and IDEAS, wherein MoSPI will provide financial assistance & data support and IDEAS will develop a desktop-based software tool to do GDP Nowcasting and a harmonised indicator framework linking administrative data on government health, nutrition and well-being schemes with household-level NSS data. This collaboration aims to deep dive into the various statistics released by MoSPI and provide harmonisation with other data sources, emphasising the data-driven decision-making initiative by the Government of India for Viksit Bharat @ 2047. **** Samrat (Release ID: 2297294) Visitor Counter : 119 Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation MoSPI signs two MoUs with IDEAS, ISI Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies Posted On:

title: PLFS introduced methodological improvements over earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation PLFS introduced methodological improvements over earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas From January 2025, survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi The Employment-Unemployment Surveys (EUS) previously conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) were the principal source of labour market statistics in the country till 2011-12. In view of the growing need for more frequent and timely labour market indicators, and based on the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission (NSC), MoSPI introduced the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in 2017 after due deliberations by expert committees constituted for developing the survey methodology and sample design. PLFS introduced methodological improvements over the earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas, Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) with in-built validation checks, collection of information on hours worked, and changes in the sampling design and schedule of enquiry to generate periodic labour force estimates. Further, from January 2025, the survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates. The concepts and definitions relating to employment, unemployment and labour force participation adopted in PLFS continue to remain consistent with those followed in the earlier EUS and are based on the recommendations of the Committee of Experts on Unemployment Estimates (Dantwala Committee) as well as the relevant international standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). Accordingly, the PLFS continues to support analysis of long-term labour market trends. Further, while disseminating the PLFS results through the Annual Reports, Quarterly Bulletins and Monthly Bulletins, MoSPI has advised users to exercise appropriate caution while making direct comparisons between PLFS and the earlier EUS estimates, as differences in survey design and methodology may influence the estimates. MoSPI continuously engages with economists, researchers, subject-matter experts and other stakeholders, and the feedback received is considered while improving survey methodology, sampling design, questionnaire design, data collection and dissemination practices to enhance the quality, reliability and relevance of labour market statistics. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Rajya Sabha today. *** Samrat (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297165) आगंतुक पटल  : 124 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Tamil Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation PLFS introduced methodological improvements over earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas From January 2025, survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin April – June, 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin April – June, 2026 Male LFPR in urban areas increased Urban UR remained stable Secondary sector employment recorded an increase in both rural and urban areas Regular wage/ salaried employees witnessed a rise प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi Snapshots of Quarterly Bulletin of  PLFS April to June 2026: · The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above was 54.6% during April–June 2026 , compared to 55.5% in the previous quarter. · The urban LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above remained unchanged at 50.2% during April–June 2026 . · The male LFPR (15 years and above) in urban areas increased marginally to 75.3% in April–June 2026 , from 75.0% in the previous quarter. · The urban Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained stable at 46.8% during April–June 2026 . · The share of regular wage/salaried employees among persons aged 15 years and above increased in both rural and urban areas, rising from 15.5% to 16.1% in rural areas and from 48.9% to 49.3% in urban areas. · The share of employment in the secondary sector for persons aged 15 years and above increased in both rural and urban areas during April–June 2026 . · The share of employment in the tertiary sector for persons aged 15 years and above recorded an increase in rural areas during April–June 2026 . · The urban Unemployment Rate (UR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7% during April–June 2026 . Introduction The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework. Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives: To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS). To extend the Quarterly PLFS results to rural areas, thereby producing quarterly estimates of labour market indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework. To provide annual estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators in both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) for rural as well as urban areas. Earlier PLFS Quarterly Bulletins released up to December, 2024, presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. The Bulletin for April – June, 2025 marked the first in the series to provide estimates for both rural and urban areas and the current Bulletin for April – June, 2026 is the fifth in the series. In this Quarterly Bulletin , efforts have been made to provide estimates of the number of workers in absolute terms . This Quarterly Bulletin presents estimates of key labour force indicators — Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR), and the distribution of workers by broad employment status and industry of work — in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), separately for rural and urban areas at the all-India level. In addition, state-level estimates of LFPR, WPR, and UR in CWS are also provided for selected States . Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS: Urban Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) remained unchanged: Overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above stood at 54.6% in the quarter April-June, 2026 as compared to 55.5% observed in the previous quarter. Rural LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above observed as 56.9% in the current quarter compared with 58.2% in the previous quarter. LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above in urban areas remained unchanged compared to the last quarter. Overall female LFPR stood at 33.2% during the current quarter compared to 34.7% in the previous quarter. The male LFPR in urban areas witnessed a marginal increase to 75.3% during the quarter from 75.0% observed in the quarter January-March, 2026. The overall LFPR during the quarter April-June, 2026 registered a modest fall of 0.4 percentage points compared to April-June, 2025. Rural LFPR is almost stable at 56.9% during the current quarter compared to 57.1% recorded during the same quarter of 2025, while the urban LFPR experienced a decrease of 0.4 percentage points. Urban LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above remains unchanged at 50.2% in April-June, 2026. Urban workforce maintains stability: Overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons of age 15 years and above estimated at 51.7% during the quarter April-June, 2026 compared to 52.8% in the previous quarter. Urban WPR for persons of age 15 years and above was stable at 46.8 % in April-June, 2026 compared to 46.9% in January-March, 2026. In urban areas, the male WPR increased marginally to 70.7% in the current quarter from 70.6% in the previous quarter, whereas the urban female WPR stood at 22.8%, compared to 23.1% in the preceding quarter. The overall WPR recorded a decline of 0.3 percentage points, from April–June, 2025 to April–June, 2026. The male WPR remained nearly unchanged during this period, while the female WPR was estimated at 31.3% in April–June, 2026, as against 31.6% in April–June, 2025. Urban WPR for persons of age15 years and above stable at 46.8% in April-June, 2026 • Overall Unemployment Rate (UR) in urban areas remained stable: Overall UR in urban areas for persons of age 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7 % during the present quarter compared to 6.6% in the previous quarter, while it edged up marginally to 4.8% in the current quarter from 4.3% in the previous quarter, in rural areas. Female urban UR decreased to 8.7% in the current quarter from 9.1% in the last quarter. In comparison to last year, in the same quarter, the UR at the person level in rural areas remained at the same level as in the present quarter (4.8%). The UR for rural male decreased to 4.8% in April-June, 2026 from 5.0% in April-June, 2025. In urban areas, the quarter-to-quarter comparison with the previous year shows stability for male and person-level UR, whereas the female UR decreased to 8.7% from 8.9%. Urban UR (age 15+ years) showed broad stability at 6.7%. Regular wage/salaried employees witnessed a rise: In rural and urban areas, engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment showed an upward movement. In rural areas, it increased to 16.1% during April-June, 2026 from 15.5% of the previous quarter, whereas in urban areas it increased to 49.3% from 48.9% during the same period. A quarter-to-quarter comparison with the same period of the previous year also indicates increased engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment from 15.4% in April-June, 2025 to 16.1% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, the engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment remained almost at the same level (49.4% vs 49.3%) during the period. Regular wage/salaried employees increased in both rural and urban areas in April-June, 2026 quarter in comparison to previous quarter Increase in employment in both secondary and tertiary sector in rural areas: Employment distribution over sector continues to follow a similar structure, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in the primary sector and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture stood at 52.9% during April - June 2026, declined from 55.8% in the previous quarter, whereas the share of employment in the tertiary sector increased from 21.7% in January - March, 2026 to 22.7% in the current quarter. The secondary sector, along with mining and quarrying, in rural areas also witnessed a rise from 22.6% in the previous quarter to 24.4% in the current quarter. In urban areas, the share of employment in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable compared to the previous quarter. The share of employment increased to 31.9% in the secondary sector along with mining and quarrying, while the agriculture sector observed a decrease to 6.1% in urban areas. In comparison to the same quarter of the previous year, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 22.1% in April-June, 2025 to 22.7% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 61.7% to 62.0% during the same period. In rural areas worker engagement in secondary sector increased to 24.4% in April-June, 2026 from 22.6% in previous quarter. Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 56.6 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter April-June, 2026, of which 40.2 crore were male and 16.4 crore were female. Persons surveyed in urban areas 2,40,881 Persons surveyed in rural areas 3,18,792 At the all-India level, the quarterly estimates are based on information collected from a total of 5,59,673 persons surveyed. The Quarterly Bulletin for the quarter April-June, 2026 is available on the website of the Ministry ( https://www.mospi.gov.in ).
