Urban WPR for persons of age 15 years and above was stable at 46.8 % in April-June, 2026 compared to 46.9% in January-March, 2026. In urban areas, the male WPR increased marginally to 70.7% in the current quarter from 70.6% in the previous quarter, whereas the urban female WPR stood at 22.8%, compared to 23.1% in the preceding quarter. The overall WPR recorded a decline of 0.3 percentage points, from April–June, 2025 to April–June, 2026. The male WPR remained nearly unchanged during this period, while the female WPR was estimated at 31.3% in April–June, 2026, as against 31.6% in April–June, 2025. Urban WPR for persons of age15 years and above stable at 46.8% in April-June, 2026 • Overall Unemployment Rate (UR) in urban areas remained stable: Overall UR in urban areas for persons of age 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7 % during the present quarter compared to 6.6% in the previous quarter, while it edged up marginally to 4.8% in the current quarter from 4.3% in the previous quarter, in rural areas. Female urban UR decreased to 8.7% in the current quarter from 9.1% in the last quarter. In comparison to last year, in the same quarter, the UR at the person level in rural areas remained at the same level as in the present quarter (4.8%). The UR for rural male decreased to 4.8% in April-June, 2026 from 5.0% in April-June, 2025. In urban areas, the quarter-to-quarter comparison with the previous year shows stability for male and person-level UR, whereas the female UR decreased to 8.7% from 8.9%. Urban UR (age 15+ years) showed broad stability at 6.7%. Regular wage/salaried employees witnessed a rise: In rural and urban areas, engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment showed an upward movement. In rural areas, it increased to 16.1% during April-June, 2026 from 15.5% of the previous quarter, whereas in urban areas it increased to 49.3% from 48.9% during the same period. A quarter-to-quarter comparison with the same period of the previous year also indicates increased engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment from 15.4% in April-June, 2025 to 16.1% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, the engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment remained almost at the same level (49.4% vs 49.3%) during the period. Regular wage/salaried employees increased in both rural and urban areas in April-June, 2026 quarter in comparison to previous quarter Increase in employment in both secondary and tertiary sector in rural areas: Employment distribution over sector continues to follow a similar structure, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in the primary sector and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture stood at 52.9% during April - June 2026, declined from 55.8% in the previous quarter, whereas the share of employment in the tertiary sector increased from 21.7% in January - March, 2026 to 22.7% in the current quarter. The secondary sector, along with mining and quarrying, in rural areas also witnessed a rise from 22.6% in the previous quarter to 24.4% in the current quarter. In urban areas, the share of employment in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable compared to the previous quarter. The share of employment increased to 31.9% in the secondary sector along with mining and quarrying, while the agriculture sector observed a decrease to 6.1% in urban areas. In comparison to the same quarter of the previous year, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 22.1% in April-June, 2025 to 22.7% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 61.7% to 62.0% during the same period. In rural areas worker engagement in secondary sector increased to 24.4% in April-June, 2026 from 22.6% in previous quarter. Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 56.6 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter April-June, 2026, of which 40.2 crore were male and 16.4 crore were female. title: Ministry of Textiles to organise IIHT SUTRA 2026 – the Inaugural National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles Ministry of Textiles to organise IIHT SUTRA 2026 – the Inaugural National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology Posted On:
                10 AUG 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, will organise IIHT SUTRA 2026 – the Inaugural National Conclave of the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology on 12 August 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), New Delhi . The conclave is being organised as a national platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge sharing among the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology (IIHTs) and their stakeholders. The Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh , will be the Chief Guest and Shri Pabitra Margherita, Minister of State for External Affairs & Textiles , will be the Guest of Honour. The programme will also be attended by Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary (Textiles) , and Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms) , along with representatives from industry, academia, research institutions, IIHT faculty, students, alumni and other stakeholders. The theme of the conclave is “IIHTs: Weaving the Future of the Indian Handloom Sector – Educate • Innovate • Transform” . The conclave seeks to provide a common national platform for the IIHTs, promote collaboration among academia, industry, research institutions and Government, showcase innovations and academic achievements, facilitate interaction among students, alumni and sector stakeholders, encourage knowledge exchange on emerging technologies, skill development and entrepreneurship, and strengthen institutional partnerships for the continued development of handloom education. A major highlight of the conclave will be the exchange of three Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Grasim Industries Limited, Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Sambalpur and Northern India Textile Research Association (NITRA) . The proposed partnerships are aimed at strengthening industry–academia collaboration, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, faculty development, internships and institutional capacity building across the IIHT ecosystem. The programme will feature the inauguration of the IIHT Exhibition and Theme Pavilion , showcasing student innovations, institutional achievements and live demonstrations . Gold Medals and Rank Certificates will be presented to meritorious IIHT students. It will also include the launch of the film “Weaving India's Handloom Future” and the release of the IIHT alumni publication “Handloom Change Makers” , highlighting the achievements and success stories of distinguished IIHT alumni. The conclave will provide an opportunity for interaction with distinguished IIHT alumni and students . An audio-visual presentation on the success stories of distinguished alumni will also be featured as part of the programme. The technical session will feature a panel discussion on “Strengthening Handloom Education through Industry–Academia Collaboration: Curriculum, Skills and Future Readiness” . The session will bring together representatives from industry, academia and other relevant institutions to deliberate on strengthening handloom education and aligning curriculum, skills and institutional capabilities with future requirements of the sector. The Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology have played a significant role in developing skilled technical manpower for the Indian handloom sector through technical education, skill development, research, design, quality improvement and technology dissemination. IIHT SUTRA 2026 seeks to build on this institutional legacy by bringing the IIHT network and its wider stakeholder ecosystem onto a common national platform for collaboration, knowledge exchange and strengthening handloom education. *** MAM/VN (Release ID: 2297320) Visitor Counter : 20 Ministry of Textiles Ministry of Textiles to organise IIHT SUTRA 2026 – the Inaugural National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology Posted On:

title: National Handloom Designers' Conclave 2026 Showcases Design-Led Innovation to Strengthen India's Handloom Sector
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles National Handloom Designers' Conclave 2026 Showcases Design-Led Innovation to Strengthen India's Handloom Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, successfully organised the National Handloom Designers' Conclave 2026 today at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The conclave brought together policymakers, eminent fashion designers, textile experts, academicians, cluster designers, master weavers, exporters, retailers and other stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening India's handloom sector through design-led innovation and market-oriented product development. The event was graced by Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, in the presence of Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ms. Amrit Raj, Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), Sh. Akhilesh Kumar, DDG, Ministry of Textiles and  other distinguished dignitaries. The dignitaries also visited an exhibition showcasing the shortlisted products developed under the National Handloom Design Contest 2026. The exhibition highlighted innovative design interventions and contemporary product development initiatives undertaken across nine handloom clusters from eight States, namely Miranchak Cluster, Purba Bardhaman Cluster, Vanitha Cluster, Dev Bhoomi Bharari Cluster, Dwarka Cluster, Khurkul Cluster, Ridrol Cluster, Imphal East, and Kondapalakala Cluster. In the inaugural address, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, noted that the future of the handloom sector rests on strong institutional support as much as on the skill of India's weavers. She highlighted the sector's role in providing livelihood to over 35 lakh persons, and the Ministry's supporting ecosystem of 29 Weavers Service Centres and 357 Handloom Cluster Development Programmes strengthening production, capacity and market linkages. She noted that 80 design-potential clusters were taken through a structured design process this year, with around 80 designers now engaged directly to help translate design into premium pricing and higher weaver incomes. She reaffirmed the Ministry's commitment to strengthening this ecosystem in the years ahead. Welcoming the dignitaries and participants, Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms), highlighted the importance of design as a catalyst for enhancing the value, competitiveness and sustainability of Indian handloom products. She underscored the Ministry's continued efforts to foster collaboration between designers and weavers, enabling traditional crafts to respond to evolving market demands. A major highlight of the conclave was the National Handloom Design Contest 2026 Prize Ceremony, where outstanding cluster designers were honoured for excellence in the Apparel, Home Furnishing, Craft Revival and Jury's Special Recognition categories. The prizes recognised outstanding design interventions that seamlessly blended traditional craftsmanship with contemporary aesthetics and evolving market preferences. The conclave featured three thematic panel discussions on  Design Innovation and Market Competitiveness, Sustainable Cluster Development and the Future of Indian Handlooms, and Design Thinking for Value Creation in Indian Handloom. Leading designers, academicians and industry experts shared insights on emerging consumer trends, sustainability, branding, exports, technology integration and strategies for enhancing the competitiveness of Indian handloom products in domestic as well as international markets. The exhibition drew an enthusiastic response from participants, offering a glimpse into innovative handloom products developed through structured design interventions across selected clusters. It showcased the immense potential of designer-weaver collaborations in creating contemporary, high-value products while safeguarding India's diverse weaving heritage. The National Handloom Designers' Conclave 2026 reaffirmed the Ministry of Textiles' commitment to positioning design as a key driver of innovation, value addition and market expansion in the handloom sector. The deliberations and knowledge shared during the conclave are expected to further strengthen the designer-weaver ecosystem, foster sustainable livelihoods and enhance the global competitiveness of Indian handloom products. *** MAM/VN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297314) आगंतुक पटल  : 38 Ministry of Textiles National Handloom Designers' Conclave 2026 Showcases Design-Led Innovation to Strengthen India's Handloom Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
